name: variant_hyphen_case
why: Spec: 'the two word lists are equal after that (e.g. "AI tools" / "ai-tools")' — hyphen becomes a space and case is lowered, so both word lists are ['ai','tools'] and both sides are plural ('tools').

name: variant_plural_noun_not_bullet
why: Spec: 'a word longer than 3 letters ending in "s" but not "ss" loses that "s"' so 'workflow' / 'workflows' is a variant, but is_bullet_variant requires 'both sides have the same grammatical number' and 'workflow' / 'workflows' → false.

name: variant_data_pipeline_plural
why: Spec lists '"data pipeline" / "data pipelines"' as a variant; but one side is plural ('pipelines' ends in s, not ss) and the other singular, so is_bullet_variant is false.

name: variant_acronym_singular
why: Spec: '"LLM" / "large language model" → true' — 'LLM' is a 2–6 capital acronym and l-l-m are the first letters of 'large language model'; both sides are singular.

name: variant_acronym_plural
why: Spec: '"LLMs" / "large language models" → true' — acronym with one lower-case 's' maps to the expansion, and both sides are plural (acronym followed by 's'; 'models' ends in s).

name: variant_acronym_number_mismatch
why: Spec: '"LLM" / "large language models" → false' for is_bullet_variant, even though is_variant is true, because a side is plural when 'its last word ends in "s"'.

name: variant_genai_near_miss
why: Spec: '"GenAI" / "generative AI" is false: "GenAI" is not all capitals' — word lists differ and no side is a pure 2–6 capital acronym.

name: variant_prompts_near_miss
why: Spec: '"prompts" / "prompt engineering" is false' — the word lists ['prompt'] and ['prompt','engineering'] differ and neither side is an acronym.

name: variant_rag_expansion
why: Spec: acronym expansion requires 'at least 2 words whose first letters (skipping the words and, of, the, for) spell the acronym's capitals' — r-a-g spells RAG, both sides singular.

name: variant_acronym_with_s_plural_mismatch
why: Spec: acronym may be 'optionally followed by one lower-case "s"' so 'RAGs' is a variant of its expansion, but 'A side is plural when ... it is an all-capital acronym followed by "s" ("LLMs")' while 'generation' is singular, so is_bullet_variant is false.

name: text_never_led_the_code_review
why: Spec: never = 'a sentence contains (case-insensitive, whole phrase: no letter right before or after) any "never" phrase of ANY entry or ANY fact'; f1 and entry e1 both carry 'led the code review'.
text: I led the code review for the team.
jd: Data analyst role: 5+ years experience with SQL. Hardelnev is our partner.
profile: 8 years in analytics; based in Boston.

name: text_never_near_miss_led_most_of
why: Spec: never phrases are matched as a 'whole phrase'; 'led most of the code review' does not contain the phrase 'led the code review', and no other rule fires (no numbers, no pairs on the matched fact).
text: I led most of the code review for the team.
jd: Data analyst role: 5+ years experience with SQL. Hardelnev is our partner.
profile: 8 years in analytics; based in Boston.

name: text_number_from_entry_dates_is_allowed
why: Spec: allowed numbers include 'the numbers in any entry's org, role or dates text' and every resume_ok fact's numbers; '2021–2023' yields the two numbers 2021 and 2023 and 3 is in f1's numbers.
text: From 2021 to 2023 I reviewed 3 pull requests per week as a data analyst.
jd: Data analyst role: 5+ years experience with SQL. Hardelnev is our partner.
profile: 8 years in analytics; based in Boston.

name: text_number_from_jd_is_allowed
why: Spec: allowed numbers include 'the numbers in the jd text'; the jd's '5+ years' normalizes to 5 (the '+' is removed as a symbol).

jd: Data analyst role: 5+ years experience with SQL. Hardelnev is our partner.
profile: 8 years in analytics; based in Boston.

name: text_number_from_profile_is_allowed
why: Spec: allowed numbers include 'the numbers in the profile text'; the profile says '8 years', so 8 is not a number problem.

name: text_phone_email_url_removed
why: Spec: 'e-mail addresses, URLs, words ending in .com/.edu/.org/.io and phone numbers like 555-010-2030' are removed before sentence splitting, so no leftover digits create a number problem.

name: text_banned_leveraged
why: Spec: banned = 'a sentence contains (whole word, case-insensitive) one of: leverage, leveraged, ...' unless the jd contains the same whole word; the jd has no 'leveraged'. The 12 is allowed because it is in f2's numbers.

name: text_banned_word_is_company_name_in_jd
why: Spec: banned words are allowed 'unless the jd text contains the same whole word (a company name such as "Hardelnev")'; the jd contains 'Dynamic'.

name: text_pair_missing_second_element
why: Spec: 'A sentence about the fact that contains a (substring) but not b is a pair problem'; f3 has pair ['70%','customers'], the sentence contains '70%' (which holds a digit, making it about the fact) but not 'customers'.

name: text_three_kinds_in_one_sentence
why: Spec: 'Each problem is reported per sentence; one sentence can produce several kinds' — 'leveraged' is banned, 9 is not in any allowed number list, and 'led the code review' is a never phrase.
